html:
SMTO-KV-0006 — A scratch note changed before the Agent could update it

GUID: f171f02a-06b8-4912-8fc1-ac02e82d7277
Slug: kv-revision-conflict
Domain: KV · Subsystem: kv

What happened

  • The Agent tried to change or remove one of its scratch notes for this Task, but that note had already changed. SMTO left the note as it was instead of overwriting it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait to see whether the Run continues. The Agent sees this error and can read the note again, then redo its change on the newest version. This conflict only means the Agent's copy of the note was out of date, and rereading it fixes that.
  2. If the Run stopped, check whether another Run in this same conversation, such as a follow-up, is still working. Let it finish or select Stop on it. A Task and its follow-ups share the same scratch notes, so two Runs can change one note at the same time.
  3. Then send a follow-up message asking the Agent to reread its scratch notes and continue. A fresh read gives the Agent the current version, so its next change is accepted.

What success looks like

  • The Run continues and its activity shows Saved task scratch data or Deleted task scratch data without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to force-overwrite the note; the newer version may hold work you still need.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Agent KV (the task scratchpad) rejected a conditional kv.put or kv.delete because expected_revision did not match the stored entry's current revision, or the entry no longer exists.

What this means

  • A conditional write/delete compares expected_revision with the current row and finds a different revision or no row. KV checks apply only to the selected conversation. Rejected validation or compare-and-set does not authorize an unconditional replacement; diagnostics do not read or mutate additional stored values.

Why this can happen

  • A conditional write/delete compares expected_revision with the current row and finds a different revision or no row.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the current exact key and revision; do not drop the precondition to force the stale write through.

How to fix it

  • Call kv.get for the key to read its current value and revision, merge deliberately, then repeat kv.put or kv.delete with that expected_revision (see KVStore._compare in src/agent_runtime/kv/store.py). Do not drop expected_revision to force an unconditional replace after another writer changed the entry.
  • Read the current value and revision, then update or delete against that exact revision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended change is rebased deliberately on the observed current value and revision.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • KV checks apply only to the selected conversation. Rejected validation or compare-and-set does not authorize an unconditional replacement; diagnostics do not read or mutate additional stored values.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-FIL-0025 — A file changed while SMTO was working with it
  • SMTO-FIL-0027 — SMTO lost its place while reading a file in parts
  • SMTO-MEM-0006 — This memory changed before your change was saved
